p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file defines the machinery of the fan-out: the committed **target manifest**, the fan-out **procedure** (fetch, verify ancestry, push fast-forward-only, report), the **fail-loud** semantics of a diverged target, the read-only **drift check**, bringing an accepted web merge **home**, why deletions and rewrites **do not propagate**, a **reference implementation**, and how to pin the never-`--force` invariant as a **test**.

manifest.title: The committed target manifest

p.THE-HOST-SET-LIVES-IN-A-SMALL-COMMITTED-: The set of hosts lives in a small **committed** file at the repo root — TOML or YAML, whatever the project already reads.

p.THE-MANIFEST-IS-REVIEWED-LIKE-CODE: It is reviewed like code, because it *is* infrastructure.

manifest.fence:
schema = 1
[[target]] name = "host-a" url = "git@host-a.example:org/project.git" mode = "push" # the maintainer pushes mainline here refs = ["main", "tags"] # what to mirror audience = "region-1"
[[target]] name = "host-b" url = "git@host-b.example:org/project.git" mode = "push" refs = ["main", "tags"] audience = "region-2"

p.A-MACHINE-LOCAL-GIT-REMOTE-CANNOT-SERVE-: A **machine-local git remote cannot serve this role.** Two reasons:

td.fact: Yes — a file CI can read
Yes — shows up in a diff

p.AUTHENTICATION-IS-THE-MAINTAINERS-PER-HO: Authentication is the maintainer's per-host keys, held in the agent or SSH config — never in the tree.

p.ADDING-A-HOST-IS-ONE-TARGET-BLOCK: Adding a host is one `[[target]]` block.

p.A-SELF-PULL-TARGET-IS-ONLY-VERIFIED: A `self-pull` target (a host that mirrors *itself* from elsewhere) is listed with `mode = "self-pull"`: the tool does not push to it, only verifies it is level with mainline.

p.FAN-OUT-PUSHES-MAINLINE-TO-EVERY-PUSH-TA: Fan-out pushes mainline to every `push` target.

p.the-shape-is-always-the-same-four-steps: The shape is always the same four steps, per target:

facts.STEP-VERIFY-ANCESTRY: **Verify ancestry** — the target's `main` must be an *ancestor* of local mainline. If it is not, the target has diverged: abort *that* target, loud (§fail-loud). Do not touch it.
facts.STEP-REPORT: **Report** the target as `ok`, `sync` (already level), or a named `DRIFT`.

p.THE-PUSH-IS-BY-URL-FROM-THE-MANIFEST: The push is **by URL**, from the manifest, so the manifest is the one source of truth for the target set — not a pile of git remotes that can drift out of step with it.

p.THE-FAN-OUT-IS-THE-ONLY-WAY-HISTORY-REAC: This is the *only* way history reaches a host: not `git push host-a`, not a click in a web UI — the fan-out.

p.A-NON-FAST-FORWARD-MEANS-THE-HOST-CARRIE: A non-fast-forward on a target means that host carries a `main` your mainline does not — almost always a direct write or a force-push to that host.

facts.RESPONSE-ABORT-THAT-TARGET: **Abort that target**, with a message naming the divergence (the host, and the commits it has that mainline lacks). *Half built: the host is named, the commits are not — by anything. This document's own reference script below aborts the target and prints `"$name: DRIFT — host has commits mainline lacks"`, which states that a divergence exists without enumerating one commit of it; and the only port in the perimeter, `xtask/src/mirror.rs`, names the failed `<target>:<ref>` pairs and relays git's rejection text (`:296-303`, `:313-320`) while performing no `ls-remote` and no `merge-base` on the push path, so it never learns the target's tip and cannot compute the range. Searched for the commit-range computation, not the wording: `merge-base` · `is-ancestor` · `ls-remote` · `rev-list` over the standing perimeter — the only `ls-remote` in the fan-out is `remote_main` (`mirror.rs:157`), reached solely from `probe` and the `self-pull` arm, and `rev-list` appears nowhere.*
facts.RESPONSE-NEVER-FORCE: **Never `--force`.** The tool has no force path to reach for.
facts.RESPONSE-DO-NOT-BLOCK-THE-OTHER-TARGETS: **Do not block the other targets.** A divergence on host B does not stop host A from receiving its legitimate fast-forward.

quote.A-DIVERGED-TARGET-IS-A-SIGNAL-TO-INVESTI: A diverged target is a signal to investigate, never something to silently clobber.

p.RECONCILIATION-IS-DELIBERATE-AND-MANUAL: Reconciliation is deliberate and manual: fetch the host, inspect the divergent commits, merge what is wanted **into mainline**, then re-fan ([`daily-loop.md` §drift](daily-loop.md#drift)).

drift-check.title: The read-only drift check

p.a-check-mode-answers-is-everyone-level: A `--check` mode answers "is everyone level?" without pushing anything:

drift-check.fence: project-mirror --check # read-only; non-zero exit on drift

p.CHECK-FETCHES-EACH-TARGET-AND-COMPARES-T: It fetches each target and compares to mainline.

p.SYNC-MEANS-LEVEL-DRIFT-NAMES-A-HOST-THAT: `sync` everywhere means all hosts equal mainline; a `DRIFT` line names a host that has moved.

p.CHECK-WRITES-NOTHING-AND-IS-SAFE-AS-A-PR: It writes nothing — safe as a pre-flight before a fan-out or inside a sweep.

bring-home.title: Bringing an accepted web merge home

p.A-WEB-MERGE-PUTS-THAT-HOSTS-MAIN-AHEAD: When a PR is merged through a host's web UI, *that host's* `main` is now ahead of mainline.

p.IT-IS-NOT-INTEGRATED-UNTIL-IT-IS-BROUGHT: It is **not integrated** until it is brought home.

p.do-that-first-then-fan-out: Do that first, then fan out:

bring-home.fence: git fetch <host-a-url> main git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD # fast-forward local mainline project-mirror # now fan out to everyone else

p.THE-FF-ONLY-IS-LOAD-BEARING: The `--ff-only` is load-bearing: if local mainline cannot fast-forward to the host's `main`, your tree has commits the host lacks, and the merge must be reconciled by hand before fan-out.

p.THE-HOST-YOU-PULLED-FROM-BECOMES-A-NO-OP: The host you pulled from becomes a no-op on the next fan-out; every other host catches up.

no-propagate.title: Deletions and history rewrites do not propagate

p.two-things-the-fan-out-will-not-carry: Two things the fan-out deliberately will **not** carry:

td.fact: An accidental deletion must not cascade to every host
The fan-out is fast-forward-only; a rewrite is a divergence, and divergences fail loud

p.DELETING-A-BRANCH-EVERYWHERE-IS-A-PER-HO: Deleting a branch everywhere is a deliberate, per-host act.

p.THE-FAN-OUT-ONLY-EVER-ADVANCES-REFS: The fan-out only ever *advances* refs, so no single mistake can subtract history from the whole fleet at once.

reference.title: Reference implementation

p.A-FAN-OUT-IS-ABOUT-FIFTEEN-LINES-OF-SH: A fan-out is about fifteen lines of `sh`.

p.THERE-IS-NO-FORCE-IN-IT-BY-LAW: There is **no `--force` in it, by law** — the absence is the invariant, not an oversight:

p.ADAPT-READ-TARGETS-TO-THE-PROJECTS-MANIF: Adapt `read_targets` to the manifest format the project uses.

p.the-two-invariants-to-preserve-when-you-: The two invariants to preserve when you port it:

facts.INVARIANT-THE-ABSENCE-OF-ANY-FORCE-PATH: and the **absence of any force path**.

never-force-test.title: Pin the invariant with a test

p.A-RULE-WITH-NO-CHECKER-IS-A-WISH: A rule with no checker is a wish.

p.build-the-push-command-in-one-place-and-: Build the push command in one place and assert, in a test or a CI step, that it can never emit a force:

never-force-test.fence: # CI guard: no force flag may appear in the fan-out script. if grep -nE -- '--force|[[:space:]]-f([[:space:]]|$)|push[^|]*\+' fanout.sh; then echo "FAIL: a force path exists in the fan-out — remove it" >&2 exit 1 fi

p.BETTER-STILL-UNIT-TEST-A-PURE-PUSH-ARGUM: Better still, in a project with a real test suite, factor the push arguments into one pure function and unit-test that its output never contains `--force`, `-f`, or a `+`-prefixed refspec for any ref shape.

p.THE-INVARIANT-IS-RUNNABLE-CAPITAL: The invariant is then **runnable capital, not a prose promise** — a rule you cannot run is a rule you cannot trust.

facts.SUM-THE-TARGET-SET-IS-A-COMMITTED-CREDEN: The target set is a committed, credential-free manifest — shared, CI-visible, reviewed like code. A local git remote cannot serve it.
facts.SUM-FAN-OUT-PER-TARGET-IS-FETCH-VERIFY-P: Fan-out per target: fetch, verify the target is an ancestor of mainline, push fast-forward-only by URL, report.
facts.SUM-A-NON-FAST-FORWARD-ABORTS-THAT-TARGE: A non-fast-forward aborts *that* target loud, names the divergence, and never forces. Reconcile into mainline by hand, then re-fan. *Three of the four are built and the fourth is half built. Loud per-target abort with the other targets still served, and a non-zero exit: `xtask/src/mirror.rs:296-320`. Never forces, and hardened past this document's ask into a unit test — `push_args` is a pure function and `push_args_never_force` (`mirror.rs:426-440`) asserts no `--force`, `-f` or `+`-refspec for four ref shapes, which `spec/common/PROP-016-source-mirrors.md:64` calls «runnable capital, not prose». «Reconcile by hand, then re-fan» is the failure message itself (`mirror.rs:315-319`). What is only half built is «names the divergence» in the sense `##RESPONSE-ABORT-THAT-TARGET` defines it: the diverged target is named, the commits it carries are not, by any implementation including this document's own reference script.*
facts.SUM-CHECK-PROBES-DRIFT-AND-A-WEB-MERGE-C: A `--check` mode probes drift read-only; bring a web merge home with `merge --ff-only` before fanning out.
facts.SUM-DELETIONS-AND-REWRITES-DO-NOT-PROPAG: Deletions and history rewrites do not propagate — a safety choice.
facts.SUM-THE-REFERENCE-FAN-OUT-HAS-NO-FORCE-P: The reference fan-out is ~15 lines with no force path; pin that absence with a test or a CI grep.
